statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-84782 ("DTLS Retransmits Handshake Messages From a Stale Buffer Offset", High): when a DTLS handshake message write is suspended part-way through and the retransmission timer fires, OpenSSL retransmits an earlier message starting from the suspended write's buffer offset, so the retransmitted message can be read past the end of the message buffer, disclosing heap memory to the peer as handshake data or crashing the process, and the retransmission overwrites the state the suspended write needs to resume. OpenSSL 3.5 is affected and fixed in OpenSSL 3.5.9. https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260929.txt, fix on the openssl-3.5 branch https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/906cf0ef1c85ca40ce69163e9086d6d3fe292943, first released in OpenSSL 3.5.9. Debian fixed it for trixie in openssl 3.5.7-1~deb13u3, DSA-6531-1: https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-84782. The DHI Debian 13 openssl packages are rebuilds of Debian's trixie openssl, published in the DHI Debian repository and the DHI enterprise repository (the FIPS builds, and the openssl-provider-fips package of every build, only in the enterprise repository); the Debian changelog shipped in each libssl3t64 package shows which Debian release a build is based on. That changelog was read from every published build on amd64 and arm64: 25 versions, 17 standard and 8 FIPS builds, based on Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2, 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, 3.5.6-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and 3.5.9-1~deb13u1. No build based on Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2, 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 or 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, FIPS builds included, names CVE-2026-84782. The first published rebuild of Debian 3.5.7-1~deb13u3, the fixed boundary here, and every later build, FIPS builds included, carry Debian's 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 entry naming it. The fix makes dtls1_handle_timeout() skip retransmission while a handshake write is suspended and makes dtls1_retransmit_message() start from the beginning of the message. In the libssl symbol table (shipped debug symbols from the libssl3t64-dbgsym package of each build), dtls1_handle_timeout() is 151 bytes on amd64 and 172 bytes on arm64 in every build before the first rebuild of Debian 3.5.7-1~deb13u3, and 174 and 200 bytes in that build and every later build, FIPS builds included. Of the FIPS providers, the openssl-provider-fips package, read from every build on both architectures, ships the OpenSSL 3.1.2 FIPS provider in the FIPS builds and the FIPS provider from the build's own OpenSSL release (3.5.5, 3.5.6, 3.5.7 or 3.5.9) in the other builds; the advisory places the affected code outside the FIPS module boundary, and the FIPS builds' libcrypto and libssl are Debian's 3.5 libraries checked above.
